archetype.name: Pretender (finishing-driven)
archetype.definition: A Seattle team whose 5-2-0 start and strong goal margin sit well ahead of a 5-on-5 shot and chance share near the bottom of the league, propped up by hot shooting and good goaltending.

report.headline: A 5-2 start built on finishing and goaltending, not on the puck
report.take:
Seattle comes into this season off three straight losing years. Last season was the worst of them by the site's measure: 34-37-11 and 31st of 32. Seven games in, the Kraken are 5-2-0, third in the Pacific, and eighth on the Teams tab. They have scored 29 goals, the offense ranks third in goals per game, and the Goal Diff / GP of 1.43 is fifth in the league. On the scoreboard this looks like a team that has turned a corner.

The underlying play says otherwise. At 5-on-5 Seattle holds a 42% share of shot attempts, 30th of 32, and a 45.7% share of expected goals, 25th. The gap between those numbers and the results is a PDO of 108.3. That is an extreme figure: the Kraken are converting at an unusual rate and getting saves on top of it. The goalies are 4.5 goals above expected, eighth in the league, with Philipp Grubauer at 4.1 of that. The listed forwards have 20 goals on 115 shots. Freddy Gaudreau has four goals on ten shots while his line holds just a 34.7% expected-goals share. The record is not built on coin flips. Pts vs Goal Diff is slightly negative, so they have won by margin. The issue is that the margin itself rests on percentages.

The schedule and history both add context. Two of the five wins are 6-1 routs of a Calgary team that is 1-5-0. The two losses came against Edmonton and Vegas, the division's best starts, by 1-3 and 2-6. The possession problem is also not new. Seattle's expected-goals share was 46.1% and 46% the last two seasons, and its Corsi share was 45% a year ago. Being out-shot is who this group has been. The A- grades for the forwards and the goaltending are real production so far, but that production is running hotter than the process behind it.

From here, the scoring should drift back toward what a sub-46% chance share usually produces. The question is how much of the banked cushion survives. Ten standings points from seven games is a real head start in a division where Vancouver, Los Angeles and Calgary have stumbled. If Grubauer and Joey Daccord keep saving goals, Seattle can hang around the playoff line. If they don't, the shot-share numbers point to a team that loses more than it wins.

strengths.title: A goaltending tandem saving real goals
strengths.body: Both goalies are above expected. Grubauer is +4.1 GSAx on a .918 save percentage and Daccord is +1.1 across four starts, putting the team eighth in Goalies GSAx. That matters more than usual for a team allowing this much possession. It is the main reason a 30th-ranked Corsi share has produced only 2.71 goals against a game. Seven games is a thin sample for goalies, so expect some give-back, but a split workload with two competent options is a sturdier base than one hot starter.

strengths.title: Scoring spread across the lineup
strengths.body: Every one of the nine listed forwards has at least three points, so this is not one line carrying the offense. Jared McCann (6.9 Game Score) and Jordan Eberle (5.5) lead it, and Chandler Stephenson has seven points with three on the power play. Depth scoring is harder for opponents to shut down than a single top unit. The rate is inflated, but the breadth of contributors should hold up even as totals cool.

concerns.title: Badly out-shot at 5-on-5
concerns.body: A 42% share of shot attempts is 30th in the league, and the expected-goals share of 45.7% is 25th. Seattle is spending most of its even-strength time defending. This is not early-season noise: last year's team posted a 45% Corsi share and a 46% expected-goals share. Until that changes, the Kraken are relying on finishing and saves to win games they are losing on the ice.

concerns.title: PDO of 108.3 will not hold
concerns.body: No team sustains a PDO this far above 100. The combination of shooting and save percentage behind Seattle's margin is the most likely thing to fade. Gaudreau's four goals on ten shots, with a 34.7% expected-goals share, are the clearest example of finishing outrunning chance creation. When the percentages normalize, the third-ranked offense should slide toward the middle of the league or lower.

concerns.title: Wingers getting loose; middling PK
concerns.body: Opposing wingers are producing above their own averages against Seattle, ranking 20th. Wingers account for 46.8% of the points the Kraken allow, against a league norm of 37.7%, which points to a coverage problem on the flanks. The penalty kill at 78.9% ranks 20th, so a team already conceding territory at 5-on-5 is not making up for it shorthanded.

trend.note: The first four games alternated wins and losses, with the losses coming against Edmonton and Vegas. Seattle has since won three straight on the road. The results are trending up even though the possession numbers are not.

weekAhead.headline: Two Florida road games against puck-hogs, then Detroit at home
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with a back end of the road trip in Tampa and Sunrise. Both are exactly the kind of opponent that exposes Seattle's weakness. Tampa Bay's 56% Corsi share and 57.6% expected-goals share are both fourth in the league. Florida's 55% shot-attempt share is fifth. Expect the Kraken to be pinned for long stretches in both games, which puts the week on Grubauer and Daccord. There is some relief in that both opponents are shooting cold, with PDOs of 98.7 and 98.8. Tampa's power play is also nearly dead at 8.3%, so Seattle's middling penalty kill may not be tested much.

Detroit at home is the softer close. The Red Wings are 1-3-2, 25th on the site, with D grades at forward and in goal and a 66.7% penalty kill. Seattle already beat them 6-3 in Detroit. Coming out of Florida with a split and then taking the Detroit game would be a good week for a team whose process trails its record.

keyMatchups.title: Tampa's possession versus Seattle's goalies
keyMatchups.body: The Lightning drive play as well as almost anyone, but their goaltending grades a C and their power play ranks 31st. If Seattle stays disciplined and gets average or better goaltending, it can steal this one despite losing the shot battle.

keyMatchups.title: Florida's net and stingy coverage
keyMatchups.body: Florida's goaltending grades an A-, and its defense holds wingers and defensemen well under their averages. That makes it the hardest test this week for Seattle's hot finishing. The opening is Florida's 75.9% penalty kill, 23rd in the league, so Seattle's 22.7% power play is its best route to goals.

keyMatchups.title: Seattle's centers against Detroit
keyMatchups.body: Detroit lets centers score well above their averages, ranking 27th, and kills only two-thirds of its penalties. Seattle dresses a center-heavy group led by Stephenson, McMann and Berkly Catton. Catton's 58.9% expected-goals share is the best on the team, which makes this the likeliest game of the week to look like a real win rather than a percentage win.

weekAhead.watch: Seattle's 5-on-5 shot share against two top-five Corsi teams. If the Kraken get buried and the saves dry up, the PDO correction starts this week.

restOfSeason.body:
The finishing and the 108.3 PDO are the parts that will regress, and the scoring rate will come down with them. The shot and chance shares are the parts most likely to persist, because they match what this franchise has produced the last two seasons. The goaltending sits in between: two goalies above expected is encouraging, but seven games say little about a full season. The 10 points already banked are real and will not be given back. A weak bottom of the Pacific also helps.

The realistic picture is a team that scores around the league average from here and gives up more than it has so far. That leaves the Kraken fighting near the wild-card line rather than holding a top-three spot. Seattle climbs past that only if the 5-on-5 numbers genuinely improve toward 50%, or if the goalies sustain a GSAx pace near the league's best.

confidence.note: Seven games, an extreme PDO, and two of the five wins against a 1-5-0 opponent.
